name: February half term
title: February half term holidays
intro: Winter sun four hours away, or snow, huskies and northern lights. Here's where to go on holiday at February half term, and what each place is like then.
seo_title: February half term holidays: where to go for sun or snow

sections.heading: When is February half term 2027?
sections.text:
Most councils in England have set February half term for **Monday 15 to Friday 19 February 2027**, so most families will travel on the weekend of 13 and 14 February. Some areas break a week earlier, and Wales and Scotland set their own dates (Cardiff, for example, has 8 to 12 February), while academies and independent schools can choose their own. Check your school's calendar before you book anything.

With only nine days including both weekends, the best half-term trips are ones where the journey doesn't eat the holiday: a flight of four or five hours at most, or a long-haul trip that's really worth it.

sections.heading: Book early, and expect to pay more
sections.text:
Half term is peak season for the two things people want in February: sun and snow. Flights to the Canary Islands and the Alps, ski lessons, and family rooms in winter-sun hotels all go up in price and sell out first. If you know where you're going, booking in the autumn usually gets the best choice.

A few ways to save:

- **Fly mid-week if your school allows**, or travel on the Sunday rather than the Saturday.
- **Look at regional airports**, which can be cheaper and less busy than London.
- **Go somewhere less obvious**: Madeira instead of Tenerife, or a smaller ski resort instead of the big names.

sections.heading: Winter sun within five hours
sections.text:
Nowhere in mainland Europe is truly warm in mid-February. For reliable sunshine you need the Atlantic islands or North Africa:

- **[Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife)** is the most reliable, with highs around 22°C in the south and very little rain. About 4 hours 15 minutes from London. Pick a hotel with a heated pool, because the sea is only around 18 to 19°C.
- **[Madeira](/destinations/madeira)** is a little cooler, at around 19 to 20°C, and greener. Better for walking than for beaches. About 3 hours 50 minutes.
- **[Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech)** has sunny days of around 20°C but cold nights. Great for a city break with a difference. About 3 hours 30 minutes.
- **[Cape Verde](/destinations/cape-verde)** is warmer again, in the mid-twenties, but often windy. About 6 hours.

Our [where is hot in February](/destinations/where-to-go-in-february) page ranks the options by temperature, rain and sunshine, and [Madeira or Tenerife](/blog/madeira-or-tenerife) compares the two most popular islands.

sections.heading: Snow: skiing and the Alps
sections.text:
February half term is the busiest week of the ski season, with good snow almost everywhere and long, bright days. The catch is crowds and prices.

- **[Chamonix](/destinations/chamonix)** is about an hour and a quarter from Geneva, which has flights from most UK airports. It's spectacular, but much of the skiing is high and challenging, so beginners should look at the gentler areas or nearby resorts.
- **Smaller and lower resorts** are cheaper and quieter at half term, though snow is less certain. Ski schools fill up fast that week, so book lessons when you book the trip.
- **[Whistler](/destinations/whistler)**, in Canada, has some of the most reliable snow anywhere, but it's a long way for one week.

If you're new to skiing, see our [adventure holidays](/destinations/adventure-holidays) page for other ideas that suit a mixed group.

sections.heading: Snow without skiing: Lapland and the northern lights
sections.text:
February is one of the best months for the far north. The days are getting longer, the snow is deep, and the nights are still dark enough for the northern lights.

- **[Rovaniemi](/destinations/rovaniemi)** in Finnish Lapland has husky and reindeer rides, snowmobiling and snowshoeing, without the Christmas crowds.
- **[Tromsø](/destinations/tromso)** in Norway is a good base for northern lights trips, fjord cruises and dog sledding. It's often milder than inland Lapland, but wetter.
- **[Reykjavik](/destinations/reykjavik)** is the easiest to reach, about 3 hours from London, with the Golden Circle and hot springs as day trips.

It's cold, often well below freezing in Lapland, so good thermals and boots matter more than anything else you pack. No one can promise the northern lights, so book a few nights and treat a sighting as a bonus.

sections.heading: City breaks
sections.text:
Cities are a good half-term choice if you'd rather keep costs down, because they're less affected by the school-holiday price rise than beach and ski trips. Choose somewhere with plenty to do indoors.

- **[Paris](/destinations/paris)** and **[Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam)** are both reachable by Eurostar, with world-class museums for cold or wet days.
- **[Rome](/destinations/rome)** is mild, around 13 to 14°C, and far quieter than in spring.
- **[Lisbon](/destinations/lisbon)** is milder still, though February can be rainy.

Our post on [the best places for a 3-day city break](/blog/best-places-for-a-3-day-city-break-in-europe) compares them by journey time and how much you can see.

sections.heading: Long-haul: worth it for a week?
sections.text:
A week is short for a long flight, but a few long-haul trips work well in February:

- **[Dubai](/destinations/dubai)** is about 7 hours away, only 4 hours ahead of the UK, and in its best season, with highs in the mid-twenties.
- **[Orlando](/destinations/orlando)** is mild and much less busy than at Easter or in summer, with highs in the low twenties. Theme park queues are shorter, though there's no guarantee of pool weather.
- **The Caribbean**, including **[Barbados](/destinations/barbados)**, is in its dry season, but flights at half term are expensive.

For more, see our [where to go in February](/destinations/where-to-go-in-february) page.

sections.heading: How to choose
sections.text:
Start with what your group wants most: warmth, snow or a city. Then check the flight time from your nearest airport, because on a short holiday an extra two hours each way matters. Finally, check the price of the week before and after, if your school's dates allow any flexibility.

If everyone wants something different, put the options on a shared list and let each person share out their points. On somewhere🎉, a draw weighted by those points picks the winner, so no one has to give in. Read more about [how it works](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday).

faqs.question: When is February half term?
faqs.answer: Usually a week in mid-February in England and Wales, often the week containing or just after 14 February. Dates vary by council and school, and Scotland's mid-term break is often shorter, so check your school's calendar.

faqs.question: Where is warm at February half term?
faqs.answer: The Canary Islands are the warmest choice within about four hours, at around 20 to 22°C. Madeira and Marrakech are a little cooler. For proper heat, Cape Verde is about six hours away and Dubai about seven.

faqs.question: Where can we go for snow at February half term?
faqs.answer: February is one of the best months for snow. The Alps, from Chamonix and Zermatt to Innsbruck and Interlaken, are in full ski season, and Lapland and Tromsø have deep snow, longer days and good odds of the northern lights.

faqs.question: Is February half term expensive?
faqs.answer: Yes, prices rise sharply in half-term week, especially for ski trips and the Canaries. Book early, and compare flights from different UK airports, as half-term dates differ by area.

faqs.question: Is February half term a good time to ski?
faqs.answer: The snow is usually good and the days are long, but it's the busiest and most expensive week of the season. Book flights, accommodation and ski lessons early.

faqs.question: Can you see the northern lights in February?
faqs.answer: Yes. February is one of the best months, with long dark nights and cold, often clear weather in Lapland and northern Norway. A sighting is never guaranteed, so stay a few nights.
